sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. (Utu = C23)
sources.note: Introduction sec. 6 (pp. viii-ix): 'The transcription is semi-phonemic', Utu fluctuating sounds listed; the words stress/accent/tone occur nowhere in the volume; C23 Utu forms carry vowel length but no stress marks (visual check of printed p. 2). Sec. 2: Silopi-Utu share >80% vocabulary.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (DOI 10.15144/PL-C19)
sources.note: Survey-wide only, sec. 1.3.3 p. 6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Utu (= language 10 'Ut') gets villages (2.21.12.17), segmental Mabuso-Stock typology (2.21.16: no voiced/voiceless stop contrast in Utu etc.), and Illustration 29 'Verb Structure in Utu' (pp. 154-155) with no stress marks; nothing on Utu stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1970. Languages of the Western Madang District. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 1271-1303. Pacific Linguistics C-13. Canberra: Australian National University. (hdl 1885/253814)
sources.note: 'Notes on the typology of the languages' (pp. 1279-1281): section A 'The Madang Phylum' (which contains Utu) lists only segmental and morphological features (absence of certain phonemes, high central vowel only in Usino, velar nasal in Kare/Urigina, no noun number, dual forms, suffixing possessive classes, suffixed tense-subject and object markers); nothing on stress, accent or tone. The sentence 'None of the languages appears to be tonal' (p. 1280, item B.3) belongs to section B, the Adelbert Range Phylum, and does not cover Utu. The words stress/accent occur nowhere in the paper; no Utu for…
